items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: which consisted of Ellie Big Ar drums and Walter Dacu playing the piano.

ctx.x: Someone say he's living, some say he's dead. In fact, I don't know, I don't know where he's in contact. Yeah, I haven't been. Wouldn't know where to contact Bob. I haven't seen Bob in about five years. But we worked all down in Buris, and then we called a place to call it down, this place down in Seminole Parish, they call it, not Buris, Delico Island. Oh yeah. We used to work down there every Saturday night, different dances, plus local around the city, different engagements like that. Then formerly I went and…

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: That was before Alec Bigard worked with him, was it or after?

ctx.x: Was that a radio all the time? Yeah, it was all stock music. And if it was in between, use music and then fake some of them, you know. Uh-huh. It was like a pure own band, it was a radio band.
That was before Alec Bigard worked with him, was it or after? Oh, it might have been after.

Because I was the first man when the Earl Roachhoe Band went in the field. He was the first man went in that band, but he was using the, let's see, he played a while with it. But that's when he come out from the Lyric Theater. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, he was doing the most field spot work. During the time of the Lyric Theater, well, he had Happy. Happy played the longest because he had a drummer named it called Zooty Singleton.
